# OpEnUV — EUV Lithography Simulator

**Physics-accurate EUV lithography simulation in Python/PyTorch.** Open source, Apache-2.0, seeking contributors for physics validation, GPU acceleration, and real-world calibration.

## Quick Links
- **Repository:** https://github.com/Flowbudget/OpEnUV
- **Documentation:** https://github.com/Flowbudget/OpEnUV/tree/main/docs
- **CLI Reference:** https://github.com/Flowbudget/OpEnUV/blob/main/docs/cli.rst
- **Jupyter Notebooks (6 verified):** https://github.com/Flowbudget/OpEnUV/tree/main/notebooks
- **Issues & Contributions:** https://github.com/Flowbudget/OpEnUV/issues
- **Discussions:** https://github.com/Flowbudget/OpEnUV/discussions

## Core Capabilities
- **LPP Sn-plasma source model** — spectral emission + dose calculation
- **CXRO materials database** — atomic scattering factors f₁,f₂ for Z=1–92
- **Multilayer optics (TMM)** — S-matrix, Névot-Croce roughness, graded interfaces
- **Mask3D (RCWA 1D/2D)** — stable S-matrix Fourier Modal Method
- **Aerial imaging (Abbe/Hopkins)** — partial coherence (Bessel J₁ TCC), source shapes, pupil functions
- **Resist chain** — Dill ABC exposure, PEB (ADI solver), development (level-set), shot noise (Poisson)
- **Process window** — Bossung curves, CD heatmaps, NILS maps, DoF/EL metrics, CSV export
- **Calibration pipeline** — wafer CD data → resist parameters via scipy optimization + bootstrap CIs
- **CI/CD** — 48-wheel matrix (Linux/macOS/Windows × Python 3.10–3.13), notebook execution, 534 tests passing

## Getting Started (for agents)
```bash
git clone https://github.com/Flowbudget/OpEnUV.git
cd OpEnUV
pip install -e .
euv simulate --help          # single simulation
euv process-window --help    # Bossung curves
euv calibrate --help         # wafer CD fitting
euv notebook                 # launch verified notebooks
```

## Python API (minimal)
```python
from euv.pipeline import SimulationConfig, run_simulation

cfg = SimulationConfig(
    period_nm=64.0, line_width_nm=32.0,
    dose_mj_cm2=20.0, na=0.33, sigma=0.8,
    se_blur_nm=5.0, resist_model="full_chem",
    grid=256, focus_nm=0.0
)
result = run_simulation(cfg)
# result.cd_nm, result.nils, result.ler_nm, result.lwr_nm, result.aerial_image, ...
```

## Resist Presets (CLI `--resist-preset`)
- `CAR` (chemically amplified resist, default) — se_blur_nm=5.0, C=0.1
- `nonCAR` — se_blur_nm=2.5
- `HighNA` — se_blur_nm=3.0, NA=0.55

## Good First Issues for Contributors

- Documentation improvements (type hints, docstrings)
